History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Adult female with 3-day history of profuse diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, and peri-umbilical abdominal pain following contact with symptomatic brother; assessment suggests infectious gastroenteritis with plan for stool culture, hydration review, and safety-net advice.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Acute diarrhoea.  
• Onset: Began 3 days ago.  
• Character: Initially very watery, now very loose.  
• Frequency: “Lost count”; ≥4 bowel motions so far today.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Feverish; feels “literally boiling,” tactile only, no thermometer used.  
  – Persistent nausea and vomiting; last emesis ~2 hours before consult after breakfast; unable to retain water, tea, or other fluids.  
  – Crampy abdominal pain centred around umbilicus; pain precedes urge to defecate, episodic.  
• No blood noted in stool or urine.  
• Urination: Passed urine ~1 hour ago; colour not assessed; frequency otherwise normal.  
• No rash reported.  
• Bowel habit prior to illness: Once daily, normal consistency; no prior similar episodes.  
• Possible trigger/contact: Brother with same symptoms; “everyone in school” reportedly affected; no recent travel.  
• Self-care to date: Oral re-hydration solution (ORS) 3×/day for 2 days; no perceived improvement due to vomiting.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions or prior abdominal surgery reported.  
• Dysmenorrhoea (managed with occasional ibuprofen).

Medications:
• Vitamin D supplement – dose/route/frequency not documented (reported as daily).  
• Ibuprofen – 200–400 mg orally PRN for menstrual cramps (exact dose/frequency not documented).  
Allergies:
• Not discussed / not documented.

Social History:
• Occupation: Graphic designer; working from home today due to illness.  
• Residence: Lives with mother and brother.  
• Smoking: Denies tobacco use.  
• Alcohol: Occasional pint; frequency not specified.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies use.

Family History:
• Brother currently acutely unwell with similar gastrointestinal symptoms (possible infectious exposure).  
• No other family history discussed.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed – telephone consultation; no vitals available.)

Investigations:
• Stool culture planned (no sample obtained yet).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral; bacterial cause to be ruled out)  
  • Arrange urgent clinic appointment for physical assessment of hydration status.  
  • Provide stool pot; send sample for microscopy, culture & sensitivity.  
  • Continue oral rehydration salts: frequent small sips.  
  • Dietary advice: bland foods (toast/biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, dairy until settling.  
  • Safety-net: attend A&E if worsening symptoms, inability to maintain oral intake, reduced urine output, persistent high fever, or new bleeding.  
  • Re-contact service anytime if concerned.

General Plan items:  
• Book appointment via support line today.  
• No antibiotics prescribed at this stage pending stool results.  
• Provide written information sheet on gastroenteritis self-care and prevention of spread (hand hygiene, separate towel use).

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: allergy status, complete medication list with doses, vitals, physical examination findings.  
● Internal conflicts: none identified.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; no major inaudible sections.
